subject: Species richness predictions: advice needed on approach

messages.author: 41a6c448d887acec
messages.subject: Species richness predictions: advice needed on approach
parts:
Hi everyone,

I’d like to invite suggestions on how to approach a piece of research. I’m trying to predict areas of higher vs. lower plant biodiversity across the island of New Guinea, on the basis of geographically very biased collection records. Having constructed various cost-distance rasters, it’s easy to see that collection is heavily skewed towards areas accessible from towns and roads. Also, a lot of older records are vaguely georeferenced. I had a couple of ideas:

1. Count the number of unique species recorded in 25x25km grids across the island, use poly2nb to construct a lattice from the grid, and build a formula for number of species ~ PCA components of environmental variables, plus the cost-distance raster, plus a spatial term as follows:

f(ID, model = "bym", graph = Lattice.adj, scale.model = TRUE,

    hyper = list(prec.unstruct = list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(1,0.001)), 

      prec.spatial =  list(prior = "loggamma", param = c(1,0.001)))

...although perhaps the cost-distance element is part of what the spatial term estimates, and hence unnecessary?

This would look a bit like a joint Species Distribution Model, although without estimating any individual species’ ranges – but we have very sparse records anyway, since people tend to record novelties and ignore common species, and I’ve had little luck with JSDMs or ensemble SDMs.

2. Since the grids are arbitrary and I have a lot of data georeferenced to within 1km, I thought maybe an inlabru mesh approach would work, with the density of records as a proxy for biodiversity once the spatial effecgt of recording effort had been accounted for, e.g.:

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(loc=speciesRecords, boundary=NGboundary, max.edge = c(25, 250), cutoff = 3,

                      crs="+proj=utm +zone=54 +south +ellps=WGS72 +units=km +no_defs")

matern <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh,

                               prior.sigma = c(1, 0.01), prior.range = c(25, 0.01))

comp <- coordinates ~

  costpath(speciesRecords$costpath, model = "linear") + # from the cost-distance raster

[....then various PCA components...] +

  mySmooth(coordinates, model = matern) + Intercept(1)

fit <- lgcp(comp, speciesRecords, samplers = NGboundary, domain = list(coordinates = mesh))

As an INLA novice I’ve been following online advice rather blindly so not even sure if the spatial modelling terms are appropriate.

In particular:

- Is there any way of separating out the spatial effect of certain areas being hard to reach, from the ‘normal’ spatial autocorrelation?

- How could I incorporate estimates of collection record coordinate uncertainty?

- Is there any way of extracting a ‘spatial field’ effect I could feed into SDM models as though it were another environmental variable?

Please do ask for more info / clarification – I don’t want to ramble on though.

Best wishes,

Michael
